overview.title: 📖 Overview: Sayings of Rav, and the Mishna of Precautions
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 11a–11b
overview.hebrewSource: לְעוֹלָם אַל יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם בְּנוֹ בֵּין הַבָּנִים
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues a chain of teachings that Rava bar Meḥasseya transmits in the name of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya in the name of Rav — practical and moral wisdom about synagogues, rulers, illness, and dreams. It then turns to a new mishna: a set of rabbinic decrees meant to keep people from carrying on Shabbat out of habit, such as a tailor going out with his needle near nightfall. The Gemara analyzes how far these 'fences' extend — to a karmelit, to an object merely stuck in clothing — and works through a contradiction in the sources about a zav's pouch.

slides.title: 💭 Rav's Maxims — What to Prefer, What to Endure
slides.subtitle: Transmitted by Rava bar Meḥasseya in the name of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav
rows: Whom to live under (best to worst)

Under Ishmael rather than a stranger (Rome); under a stranger rather than a Ḥabar (Persian fire priest); under a Ḥabar rather than a Torah scholar; under a Torah scholar rather than an orphan or widow
What to endure (any X but not Y)
Any illness but not intestinal disease; any pain but not heart pain; any ache but not headache; any evil but not an evil wife

Any city whose houses' roofs are higher than the synagogue is ultimately destroyed (Ezra 9:9) — Rav Ashi credited building Mata Meḥasseya's synagogue tall, though it was later destroyed for a different sin

callout.label: The reach of government:
callout.text: Rav: 'Even if all seas were ink, reeds were quills, and the heavens were parchment, it would not suffice to write the full scope of governmental affairs' (alluded to in Proverbs 25:3).

slides.title: 😴 A Fast to Undo a Bad Dream
slides.subtitle: Rav, Rav Ḥisda, and Rav Yosef refine the remedy

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav: A fast is as effective against a bad dream as fire is to chaff
2️⃣ Rav Ḥisda adds: only if held on that very day of the dream
3️⃣ Rav Yosef adds further: one may even hold this fast on Shabbat itself
4️⃣ Case in point: Rav Yehoshua, son of Rav Idi, refused a fine third-born calf at Rav Ashi's table, explaining that a dream-fast — unlike an ordinary fast — cannot simply be postponed to another day

slides.title: 📚 Interrupting Torah Study for Shema and Prayer
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yoḥanan qualifies a baraita's ruling

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: Torah scholars engaged in study stop for Shema, but do not stop for prayer.

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: That was only taught for the likes of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai and his colleagues, whose Torah study is their sole vocation.

lines.speaker: By contrast
lines.text: For the likes of us, who also engage in other pursuits, we stop our study for both Shema and prayer.

lines.speaker: Exception
lines.text: The Elders of Hagronya, quoting Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok: 'When we were engaged in intercalating the year in Yavne, we stopped for neither Shema nor prayer' — that work was too urgent to interrupt.

slides.title: 🧵 The Mishna's Fences Against Carrying Out of Habit
slides.subtitle: Decrees issued so a person will not forget and violate Shabbat

nodes.content: ❓ Mishna: near nightfall on Shabbat eve, a tailor may not go out with his needle, nor a scribe with his quill
💡 Reason: lest he forget it is Shabbat and carry it into the public domain

columns.label: Same mishna
columns.content: One may not shake lice from clothing, nor read by candlelight, lest one adjust the wick

columns.label: Parallel decree
columns.content: A zav may not eat with the zava, lest familiarity lead to sin

nodes.content: ⚖️ Gemara: does this same 'fence upon a fence' extend to drinking across a karmelit? Abaye: yes, it is treated the same as private/public domain. Rava: no — one does not build a rabbinic fence to protect another rabbinic decree

slides.title: 🪡 The Needle — Held in Hand, or Stuck in Cloth?
slides.subtitle: The manner of carrying determines liability, echoed in the zav's pouch

boxes.title: Held in the hand
items: The typical way of carrying — a full-fledged act by Torah law
All agree the mishna's ban near dusk applies here

boxes.title: Stuck in clothing
items: Not the typical manner — only a rabbinic shevut
Rabbi Meir: exempt by Torah law, even for a craftsman
Rabbi Yehuda: a craftsman who carries in his craft's own typical manner is liable

boxes.title: The zav's pouch (parallel case)
items: Two baraitot conflict — one exempts, one obligates a sin-offering
Resolved by Rav Yosef as Rabbi Meir vs. Rabbi Yehuda, or by Rav Hamnuna as a zav with two sightings (needs the pouch) vs. three (does not)

summary.principle: Alongside Rav's practical wisdom about neighbors, illness, and dreams, the mishna's decrees on Shabbat eve show how the Sages built precautions to keep habit from leading a person into carrying — and the Gemara carefully maps how far each fence extends.

flowSteps.content: 💭 Rav's maxims: whom to live under, what illness to prefer, a city's rooftops
😴 A fast undoes a bad dream 'like fire to chaff' — even on Shabbat, per Rav Yosef

columns.content: 📚 Torah scholars stop for Shema always, for prayer only if Torah is not their sole vocation
🧵 Tailor's needle, scribe's quill: no going out near dusk, lest one forget

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: A rabbinic fence may itself need a further fence — but Rava holds one decree need not protect another

quiz.q: According to Rav's ranking of whom it is preferable to live under, which is considered worst of all?
o: A stranger (Rome)
A Ḥabar (Persian fire priest)
A Torah scholar
An orphan or a widow
quiz.e: Rav's chain ends: 'under a Torah scholar and not under an orphan or widow,' since God is especially attentive to their cries when wronged.

quiz.q: According to Rav Ḥisda, when must a fast to counter a bad dream be held to be effective?
o: Within thirty days of the dream
On that very day of the dream
Any day before the following Shabbat
Only on a public fast day
quiz.e: Rav Ḥisda specified that the remedy of fasting works specifically 'on that day' — and Rav Yosef added that this may even be done on Shabbat itself.

quiz.q: Rabbi Yoḥanan limits the baraita's exemption from stopping Torah study for prayer to whom?
o: Only the litigants in a court case
The likes of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai and his colleagues, whose Torah is their sole vocation
Anyone currently intercalating the calendar
Every Torah scholar without exception
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan taught that ordinary people ('the likes of us') must stop for both Shema and prayer; only those whose Torah study is their entire occupation need not stop for prayer.

quiz.q: Why does the mishna forbid a tailor from going out with his needle near nightfall on Shabbat eve?
o: Because sewing itself is forbidden that close to Shabbat
Lest he forget he is carrying it and go out with it into the public domain after Shabbat begins
Because needles were considered unclean vessels
To prevent him from working past the time for prayer
quiz.e: The mishna's concern is habit: he may forget the needle is on him and carry it out once Shabbat has begun.

quiz.q: Why does Rava permit drinking from one domain while standing in a karmelit, against Abaye's view?
o: Because a karmelit is treated exactly like a public domain
Because the prohibition on a karmelit is itself only a rabbinic decree, and the Sages do not issue one decree to safeguard another decree
Because drinking is never considered an act of carrying
Because Rava holds karmelit does not exist as a category
quiz.e: Rava's reasoning is that since the karmelit restriction is itself rabbinic, it would be excessive to add a further rabbinic fence around it.
